title: "The Mind-Energy law and the third power"
description: >
  Why mental energy scales as 1/τ³, and what a log-log check across five states
  shows.
date: 2026-07-14
categories: [RTC, Mind-Energy, mathematics]

## The law

The Mind-Energy law states that mental energy scales inversely with the third
power of the perceptual time threshold:

$$E_m = \frac{1}{\tau^3}$$

The threshold $\tau$ is the shortest interval within which two stimuli are still
experienced as one moment. The exponent 3 is not a free parameter: it follows
from the assumption that the perceptual field can divide along three independent
directions, and that energy per direction runs linearly with the sampling rate
$1/\tau$.

## A check across five states


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tau <- c(0.100, 0.080, 0.062, 0.050, 0.042)
Em  <- 1 / tau^3
fit <- lm(log(Em) ~ log(tau))
summary(fit)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}


The slope comes out at -3; deviations larger than
0.1 in practice point to a measurement error in $\tau$, not an error in the law.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(log(tau), log(Em), pch = 19, col = "#0099c8",
     xlab = "ln tau", ylab = "ln Em")
abline(fit, col = "#00549c")
```

The full calculation ships as a module in [the suite](../../suite.qmd). Run it
there and download the table as CSV.

## What it does not say

The law describes a scaling relation, not an absolute quantity. Without a
calibrated unit for $E_m$ only the ratio between two states carries meaning —
which is exactly what the log-log form makes measurable.
